restrictions: Generic birthday collision search over N=2^128 fresh independent uniform 55-byte messages; the coins are the message draws and the target is fixed.

Each complete 31-round SHA-256 hash (fixed IV, steps 0..30 on one padded block, feed-forward, full 256-bit digest) is computed by CHARGED WORD OPERATIONS (1850 per message), not by invoking the one-unit compression primitive; the only one-unit charges are the two whole compressions of the single final verification.
Collisions are detected on the full 256-bit digest with a Briggs-Torczon sparse-set table (sparse index width s=160); memory is reported only and does not affect the scalar.

Success probability at least 0.39 is proved DISTRIBUTION-FREE for the fixed target (no random-function, ideal-hash, or round-independence premise); one supporting heuristic H-IDX bounds only detection work (the 2^-33 F2 term), not success.
One run, no restart; all draws, failed and discarded messages, table work and verification are charged. No certificate, experiment, precomputed collision, or nonuniform advice.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over an established attack or security bound.

heuristics.statement: The top s=160 bits of the complete 31-round SHA-256 digest distribute the N=2^128 evaluated messages with bounded clustering, so the expected number of sparse-set slot events (F2, F4) is within a constant factor of the uniform value. Used only to bound detection work and the 2^-33 F2 term; the dominant success terms are distribution-free and the dominant time term is the deterministic 1850-operation body.
heuristics.scope: The at most N=2^128 digest evaluations of one run on the fixed complete 31-round SHA-256 map (target sha256-r31-prefix-v1).
heuristics.extrapolation: From the standard behaviour of a cryptographic digest's high bits as a balanced hash index to this specific 31-round map; no ideal behaviour is claimed, and the scalar's sensitivity to H-IDX is below 2^-33.
heuristics.limitations: A modelling assumption used ONLY for detection-structure work and the F2 term; success probability's dominant terms (F1, FR) are distribution-free and the time bound's dominant term is deterministic, so H-IDX cannot materially change the claimed scalar.
